spans.claim: Mayor John Wallingford was found dead in the Mayor's Parlour
spans.anchor: found Wallingford lying across his desk, dead
spans.span: He detailed the particulars of his own coming to the town on the evening of the murder, and told how he and Bunning, going upstairs to the Mayor's Parlour, had found Wallingford lying across his desk, dead.

spans.claim: The murder weapon was a rapier found behind the bookcase
spans.anchor: long, thin, highly polished rapier
spans.span: And with a jerk of his wrist he drew from the brown paper a long, thin, highly polished rapier, the highly burnished steel of which was dulled along half its length, as if it had been first dimmed and then hastily rubbed.

spans.claim: A blood-stained cambric handkerchief was found partially burnt on the hearth
spans.anchor: blood-stained, charred, cambric pocket-handkerchief

spans.claim: Dr. Wellesley admitted the handkerchief was his
spans.anchor: that is certainly part of a handkerchief of mine
spans.span: that is certainly part of a handkerchief of mine.

spans.claim: Dr. Wellesley was absent from his surgery for nineteen minutes
spans.anchor: he went out of the surgery... half-past seven to eleven minutes to eight

spans.claim: Secret passage exists between St. Lawrence tower and Moot Hall
spans.anchor: secret passage through the apparently solid arch in St. Lawrence Lane
spans.span: Pellery, comes to this--there is a secret passage through the apparently solid arch in St. Lawrence Lane which leads direct from the middle chamber in St.

spans.claim: Krevin Crood obtained keys to St. Lawrence church and used secret passage
spans.anchor: I called at Spizey's cottage in St. Lawrence churchyard and got the keys
spans.span: About seven o'clock of the evening on which Wallingford was murdered, I called at Spizey's cottage in St. Lawrence churchyard and got the keys of the church from him, on the excuse that I wanted to copy an inscription.

spans.claim: Krevin overheard quarrel between Wallingford and Mrs. Saumarez
spans.anchor: Wallingford was not alone. He had a woman with him
spans.span: Wallingford was not alone. He had a woman with him.

spans.claim: Mrs. Saumarez stabbed Wallingford with the rapier
spans.anchor: she had snatched up that rapier and run him through

spans.claim: Krevin Crood wiped blood with handkerchief and burned it partially
spans.anchor: I pulled out my handkerchief... and threw the handkerchief in the fire

spans.claim: Krevin Crood took Wallingford's papers and memorandum book
spans.anchor: I took up a mass of papers and a memorandum book which Wallingford had laid down
spans.span: Then I took up a mass of papers and a memorandum book which Wallingford had laid down--and went away by the passage.

spans.claim: Typewritten threatening letter was typed on Simon Crood's machine
spans.anchor: the broken letters... all on Uncle Simon's machine

spans.claim: Louisa Speck identified the handkerchief as the one missing from Mallett's drawer
spans.anchor: I noticed then that the handkerchief had gone
spans.span: I noticed then that the handkerchief had gone.

spans.claim: Krevin Crood confessed the truth in court
spans.anchor: I did not kill Wallingford, and accordingly my brother could not be an accessory
spans.span: The police, as usual, are absolutely and entirely at fault--I did not kill Wallingford, and accordingly my brother could not be an accessory to what I did not do and never had the remotest intention of doing.

spans.claim: Mrs. Saumarez is the actual murderer
spans.anchor: Who was she, then? ... Mrs. Saumarez!

spans.claim: The memorandum book with Wallingford's notes was found at Krevin Crood's lodgings
spans.anchor: I there found in an old writing-case... papers in the handwriting of the late Mayor

spans.claim: The Local Government Board inquiry was a farce manipulated by Town Trustees
spans.anchor: I have resigned my appointment... I know the financial affairs of the borough are rotten-ripe

spans.claim: Mrs. Mallett fled town due to her husband's affair with Mrs. Saumarez
spans.anchor: Mrs. Mallett has left her husband
spans.span: Now, to begin with, I suppose you have both heard--it's pretty well known through the town, I understand--that Mrs. Mallett has left her husband?

spans.claim: The secret passage door panel slides back easily
spans.anchor: The panelling... slides back, and gives access to a passage

spans.claim: Krevin Crood used the secret passage to enter the Mayor's Parlour
spans.anchor: I slipped open the panel, and crossed over to the Moot Hall
